deep.reconstruction:
Context. This leaf is a draft of Riemann's Inaugural-Dissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen fuer eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veraenderlichen complexen Groesse', Art. 10 (end) and the start of Art. 11. Here it is labelled '§. 11'. The whole page is struck through with one diagonal pencil line, which shows that it was superseded or copied out. The setting is a domain T lying simply (schlicht) over the plane A. u is a real function with Delta u = 0 'allgemein zu reden', i.e. apart from exceptional points. p denotes the normal pointing into the region, s is arc length, O_0 = (x0, y0) is an interior point, and r = |(x,y) - (x0,y0)|.

Step 1 (end of the Green-identity computation begun on the previous leaf of the draft). Green's second identity is applied to u and log r on T minus a small disc of radius r about O_0. The contribution of the small circle is computed with ds = r dphi and d(log r)/dr = 1/r. It equals -Int_0^{2pi} u (d log r/dr) r dphi - log r Int (du/dp) ds. By an earlier article, the flux Int (du/dp) ds over a closed curve vanishes when Delta u = 0 inside it. So the circle term is -Int_0^{2pi} u dphi. If u is continuous at O_0 this tends to -2 pi u_0 as r -> 0.

Step 2. The boundary integral plus the circle integral equals 0. This gives two formulas.
(i) Green's representation formula: u_0 = (1/2pi) Int_{boundary of T} (log r du/dp - u d(log r)/dp) ds, with p the inward normal.
(ii) Gauss's mean-value formula: u_0 = (1/2pi) Int_0^{2pi} u dphi over any circle about O_0 inside T. This holds because the boundary of a disc may itself be taken as the boundary.
[My check of the sign convention: take u = 1 on the disc of radius R about O_0. Then du/dp = 0 and d(log r)/dp = -1/R, so the formula gives 1. Correct.]

Step 3. Lehrsatz (a removable-singularity and regularity theorem for harmonic functions). Suppose u satisfies u_xx + u_yy = 0 on T, apart from exceptional points such that:
1) the points where the equation fails do not fill any area;
2) the points where u, u_x, u_y are discontinuous do not fill any line;
3) at each discontinuity point, rho*u_x and rho*u_y -> 0 as the distance rho -> 0.
Then u, together with all its derivatives, is finite and continuous at every interior point of T. The only exceptions are arbitrary changes of value at isolated points, i.e. removable discontinuities, which are excluded by convention.
[Implicit step, mine: condition 3 makes the small circles around exceptional points contribute nothing. The term log rho * rho * du/dp -> 0. Also u = o(log(1/rho)), so the term u * rho * (1/r) stays harmless. Hence the representation in Step 2 is valid regardless of the exceptional points.]
Proof. Let O_0 move. In the boundary integral only log r and its derivatives with respect to x0 and y0 depend on O_0. For a fixed boundary element and O_0 interior these are finite and continuous. All their derivatives are rational functions with only powers of r in the denominator. So the integral, and hence u_0, is C-infinity in (x0, y0). The right-margin additions refine the wording: the only conceivable failure, discontinuity at single points that can be cured by redefining values there, is excluded by hypothesis (condition 3 / convention).

Step 4 (§11 begins). From the mean-value identity Int_0^{2pi} (u - u_0) dphi = 0, u - u_0 cannot be one-signed and nonzero on part of a circle about an interior point. This is the lead-in to the maximum principle and the identity theorem on the next page (Theorems I-III).
errors: Sign of the log r * Int(du/dp)ds term on the small circle depends on the normal convention. As written ('-log r Int du/dp ds') it conflicts with p = inward normal of the region, which would give '+'. This is immaterial because the flux integral vanishes.

The claim 'finite and continuous with all derivatives' is justified by differentiating under the integral. That needs the boundary integral to be well defined, e.g. u and du/dp integrable on the boundary. This is tacit, standard for the period.

Condition 3 alone gives u = o(log 1/rho) near a singular point, which suffices. Riemann does not spell out why the small circles around singular points contribute nothing here. Presumably this is covered in the preceding article.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: read roughly '[Winkel], welchen wir durch phi bezeichnen' rather than '[?]welches durch phi bezeichnen'.
'einer veraenderlichen der Ebene A' should be 'eine ... die Ebene A allenthalben nur einfach bedeckenden Flaeche T'.
'allgemein genuege der Differentialgleichung' should be 'allgemein zu reden der Differentialgleichung ... genuegt'.
In §11 the formula should read 'Int_0^{2pi}(u-u_0) dphi = 0'.
Margin last lines: 'die Vorsaetze [?] unseres Lehrsatzes' is probably 'die Voraussetzung 3. unseres Lehrsatzes ausgeschlossen ist'.
Margin: 'fuer die Stetigkeit[?]' is uncertain. The intended sense is that removable single-point discontinuities are excluded.
